question: Does a per-task class-balanced LightGBM on a shared PCA representation beat a standard shared-hidden-layer MLP on every related classification task, not just on average, using scikit-learn's digits data?
method: Derive three binary tasks (is-even, is-greater-than-4, is-prime) from the digit label. One stratified 70/30 split. Compare a shared-hidden-layer MLP with a shared PCA + per-task class-balanced LightGBM. Hyper-parameters chosen by 5-fold CV on train only; test used once. Seeds 42, 43, 44.
metric_name: macro-F1 averaged over 3 binary tasks (is_even, is_gt_4, is_prime)
baseline: Standard hard-parameter-sharing MLP: one shared hidden layer, sigmoid multi-label outputs (sklearn MLPClassifier) on standardised pixels; hidden size and alpha chosen by train-only CV.
improved: Shared PCA representation (30 components fit on training pixels) with a separate class-balanced LightGBM per task; num_leaves, learning_rate and n_estimators chosen per task by train-only CV.
notes: Only one train/test split is used, so split-to-split variance is not measured; seeds capture model randomness only. The three tasks are deterministic functions of one label and therefore strongly related; the test set is small, so per-task gaps of a few points may be noise. Both models get the same 5-fold CV folds per seed; the baseline grid has 4 configurations and the LightGBM grid has 8 per task. PCA dimension is fixed, not tuned. The paper's architecture is not specified in the provided abstract, so this is not a replication of its method. load_digits is bundled, so no network download or retry logic is needed.
